answers.answer: Each player takes only their chosen hero’s matching components. Set dials to the listed starting health (undialed sidekicks have 1); shuffle the 30 action cards into a separate face-down deck and draw 5. The younger player places their hero on space 1, then sidekicks in separate spaces sharing a zone with that hero; if the hero space has several zones, any of them is allowed. The older player then does the same on space 2. Choose Alice’s BIG or SMALL size at setup when placing her. Younger player takes the first turn.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2–6: “younger player places their hero on starting space 1” then sidekicks in “separate spaces sharing a zone”; older player uses space 2; Alice size chosen at setup; younger player first. Setup step 3: shuffle 30 and draw 5.

answers.answer: Take 2 actions from maneuver, scheme, and attack. You may repeat an action, including maneuver twice, but cannot skip an action. You may hold more than 7 cards during your turn; at turn end discard to your own discard pile until you have 7. If you temporarily have 9, discard 2 at the end of your turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “take 2 actions”; “You may repeat an action”; “you cannot skip an action”; “At the end of your turn, discard excess cards … until you have 7.”

answers.answer: Maneuver first draws 1 card, mandatory, then each fighter may move up to that player’s move value plus applicable bonuses; each may choose zero. Movement follows adjacent connecting spaces. You may pass through friendly fighters but cannot finish in an occupied space, and may not pass through opposing fighters. Choose fighter order and finish one fighter’s movement before starting another’s; you cannot interleave their moves.
answers.evidence: Maneuver: “Draw 1 card first, mandatory”; then optionally move each fighter one at a time, “up to your move value,” including zero; ordinary movement restrictions; “finish one fighter’s movement before starting another’s.”

answers.answer: During a maneuver, discard 1 hand card and add its printed BOOST value to the movement value for that maneuver; ignore the discarded card’s effects. Every one of your fighters receives that allowance. A card unusable because its fighter is defeated can still be discarded to BOOST.
answers.evidence: BOOST movement: discard 1 card to add its BOOST value; “Ignore the discarded card’s effects”; “Each of your fighters receives that allowance”; defeated-fighter card “can still be discarded to BOOST.”

answers.answer: Do not reshuffle and do not decline a mandatory draw. With the deck empty, each missing card causes each of your fighters to take 2 damage. Drawing 2 with no cards causes two separate 2-damage events: 4 total damage to the surviving hero and 4 to the surviving sidekick.
answers.evidence: Empty deck: “Do not reshuffle”; each time you must draw and cannot, “each of your fighters immediately takes 2 damage instead”; mandatory draw of 2 causes two separate events.

answers.answer: Any fighter may attack an adjacent opponent, including across zone boundaries. Thus both melee and ranged fighters can target an adjacent opponent across a boundary. Melee cannot attack a nonadjacent target, even in the same zone. Ranged can attack a nonadjacent opponent sharing a zone, including in a disconnected part of that colored zone.
answers.evidence: Attack declaration: “Any fighter may attack an adjacent opponent, even across zone boundaries”; melee only adjacent; ranged may attack any opponent sharing a zone regardless of distance or adjacency, including a separated part.

answers.answer: An attack action is illegal if you lack an attack-capable card in hand or have no valid target for one of your fighters. Declare the attacking (active) fighter and the opposing target. The attacker plays an attack card legal for that fighter; the defender may decline or play a legal defense card for the defending fighter. Reveal chosen cards simultaneously. Versatile cards may attack or defend and count as both attack and defense cards for other effects; pure attack cards cannot defend and pure defense cards cannot initiate attacks.
answers.evidence: Attack: no attack action without attack-capable card or valid target; declaration and legal face-down cards; defender may decline; simultaneous reveal. Card types: versatile count as both for other effects.

answers.answer: Resolve immediately effects, then during-combat effects, then calculate attack damage (attack minus defense, minimum zero; with no defense use full attack value) and reduce health. Next resolve after-combat card effects, then other after-combat game effects such as a hero ability, then put played cards in their owners’ discard piles. At any shared timing, defender’s effect resolves first. Effects are mandatory unless they say otherwise, and are completed in printed order.
answers.evidence: Combat timing list 1–6; “Whenever effects share a timing, the defender’s effect resolves first”; effects mandatory unless they say otherwise.

answers.answer: The 4-versus-4 attack deals no attack damage, so the defender wins combat; the later 2 damage from a card effect does not change the winner. With no defense card against attack value 4, the defender takes 4 attack damage.
answers.evidence: Combat result: attack value minus defense, minimum zero; no defense means attack value. “Winning combat” depends only on the attack itself dealing at least 1; effect damage does not change winner.

answers.answer: If the sidekick reaches zero while its hero survives, the sidekick is defeated and its token is immediately removed; its played card’s after-combat effect still resolves unless the game has already ended. If a hero reaches zero, that hero immediately loses and the game ends, so do not continue pending effects to heal the hero or finish the turn.
answers.evidence: Scoring: zero-health fighter is defeated; immediately remove defeated sidekick token; defeated fighter’s played card still resolves after combat unless game already ended. Hero defeat immediately ends game; do not continue pending effects to heal.

answers.answer: Play a scheme face up from hand, declaring an eligible fighter as active; resolve its effect, then put it in your discard pile. You cannot play it if its listed fighter(s) are defeated. Both players may inspect either discard pile at any time.
answers.evidence: Scheme: face up, declare fighter allowed by its label, resolve, then discard; cannot play if listed fighters defeated. Discard piles: both players may inspect either “at any time.”

answers.answer: Alice has 13 health, move 2, and a melee attack. Jabberwock has 8 health and melee attack. Choose Alice BIG or SMALL when placing her at setup. BIG adds 2 to Alice’s attack-card values; SMALL adds 1 to her defense-card values, including versatile cards when used in that role. Neither bonus applies to Jabberwock.
answers.evidence: Fighter reference lists Alice 13, melee, move 2; Jabberwock 8, melee. Alice ability specifies setup choice and bonuses, and says “These bonuses belong to Alice, not Jabberwock.”

answers.answer: Arthur has 18 health and melee attack; Merlin has 7 health and ranged attack. When Arthur attacks, he may play a hand card face down alongside his attack card and add that card’s BOOST value, ignoring its effects; discard the BOOST card. If the opponent cancels effects on Arthur’s attack card, his ability BOOST is discarded without effect.
answers.evidence: Fighter reference: Arthur 18 melee; Merlin 7 ranged. Arthur ability: when he attacks, may BOOST by playing a face-down hand card alongside; if attack-card effects are canceled, BOOST is discarded without effect.

answers.answer: Medusa has 16 health, move 3, and ranged attack. She has 3 Harpies, each with 1 health and melee attack. At the start of Medusa’s turn, she may optionally deal 1 damage to one opposing fighter in Medusa’s zone; adjacency is not required.
answers.evidence: Fighter reference lists Medusa and Harpy stats. Medusa ability: “at the start of your turn,” “may deal 1 damage” to one opposing fighter in her zone; no adjacency requirement.

answers.answer: Sinbad has 15 health and melee attack; Porter has 6 health and melee attack; normal move is 2. With 3 Voyages in Sinbad’s discard pile, each may move 2 + 3 = 5 spaces in a maneuver before any maneuver BOOST. A newly played base-2 Voyage has combat value 2 + 3 other Voyages already in the discard pile = 5 before other modifiers; it does not count itself because it enters the discard pile only at the end of combat.
answers.evidence: Fighter reference lists Sinbad and Porter stats and move 2. Sinbad ability gives each fighter +1 per Voyage in discard; Voyage attacks +1 per other Voyage there, and the current card is not in discard until end of combat.

answers.answer: Eat Me is a scheme: move Alice up to 3 spaces, then change size. Drink Me is a scheme: draw 2 cards, then change size. The size change is not optional: the card descriptions state it without “may,” and card effects are mandatory unless they say otherwise.
answers.evidence: Alice card reference: Eat Me “Move Alice up to 3 spaces, then change size”; Drink Me “Draw 2 cards, then change size.” General rule: effects mandatory unless otherwise stated.

answers.answer: Jaws That Bite attacks at 4 against Skirmish at 4, so the attack deals 0 damage and Arthur wins combat as defender. At the shared after-combat timing, defender-first priority lets Arthur resolve Skirmish first; because Arthur won, he may move one fighter in that combat up to 2 spaces. Given that he moves Jabberwock away and no fighter remains adjacent to Jabberwock, Jaws deals no damage. If a friendly fighter alone were adjacent, Jaws would still deal 2 damage to it; Alice cannot decline, because the effect is mandatory and includes a friendly fighter if that is the only choice.
answers.evidence: Timing example explicitly describes Jaws vs Arthur’s Skirmish at 4 vs 4, defender wins, defender-first Skirmish can move Jabberwock away, and Jaws then deals no damage if no adjacent fighter. Jaws effect: 2 to any fighter adjacent, including friendly if only choice; mandatory effects.

answers.answer: At 4 health, Arthur is at 4 or less and not defeated, so set his health to 8. At 5 health, nothing happens. At 0, the duel has already ended, so the card cannot heal him. Recovery cannot raise a fighter above the maximum on that fighter’s dial.
answers.evidence: Holy Grail: at 4 or less but not defeated set health to 8; at 5+ nothing; at 0 duel already ended. Recovery cannot exceed dial maximum.

answers.answer: Winged Frenzy moves each of Medusa’s fighters up to 3 spaces and allows them to pass through opposing fighters. Afterward, return one defeated Harpy, if any, to any unoccupied space in Medusa’s zone. It cannot end on an occupied space.
answers.evidence: Winged Frenzy: “Move each of your fighters up to 3 spaces; they may pass through opposing fighters”; then return a defeated Harpy, if any, to an unoccupied space in Medusa’s zone. Movement/place rule retains one fighter per space.

answers.answer: With 4 other Voyages in the discard pile, Voyage Home’s combat value is 2 + 4 = 6. After combat, take all other Voyage cards from the discard pile into hand; Voyage Home itself is excluded from that retrieval and goes to the discard pile at the normal end of combat. The four retrieved cards leave one Voyage (Home) in the discard pile, so the next unboosted maneuver allowance is 2 + 1 = 3 spaces for each of Sinbad’s fighters.
answers.evidence: Each Voyage is Sinbad-only attack value 2 and adds +1 for each other Voyage in discard. Voyage Home takes all other Voyage cards from discard into hand; Home itself goes to discard at end of combat. Maneuver bonus is +1 per Voyage in discard.
